chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Martyrdom in the way of God, Exalted and Mighty, is expiation for every sin except for debt, for which there is no expiation other than its payment, or the debtor settling it, or the creditor forgiving it.

key_terms.الْقَتْلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: Martyrdom in the way of God

ai.seo_question: Does martyrdom erase all sins including financial debts?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that while martyrdom expiates all personal sins against God, it does not absolve financial debts, which are rights of other people (Huquq al-Nas). This distinction underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the creditor's right must be satisfied through the deceased's estate, payment by heirs, or voluntary forgiveness, preserving the integrity of social contracts even in the face of spiritual elevation.
